entities.summary: Walter Marty Schirra Jr. was an American naval aviator, test pilot, and NASA astronaut. In 1959, he became one of the original seven astronauts chosen for Project Mercury, which was the United States' first effort to put humans into space. On October 3, 1962, he flew the six-orbit, nine-hour, Mercury-Atlas 8 mission, in a spacecraft he nicknamed Sigma 7, becoming the fifth American and ninth human to travel into space. In December 1965, as part of the two-man Gemini program, he achieved the first space rendezvous, station-keeping his Gemini 6A spacecraft within 1 foot (30 cm) of the sister Gemini 7 spacecraft.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the original seven astronauts chosen for Project Mercury and a key figure in the Gemini program, Wally Schirra played a crucial role in advancing human spaceflight capabilities. His achievements, including the first space rendezvous, paved the way for future space exploration.
